newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - McDonald's U.S. income won't hit goal.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - McDonald's U.S. income won't hit goal.

text.p: McDonald's Corp, which said it is still on track for record earnings in 1997, said U.S. operating income this year will not reach its target of a mid-single-digit percentage growth rate.

"Our objective long-term is to grow the U.S. (operating income) hopefully in the mid-single-digit rate," McDonald's Chief Financial Officer Michael Conley said in an interview. "We're not on track with that for this year."
The fast-food giant has called 1997 a "transition year" for its U.S. business.

McDonald's objectives are to grow international operating income at a compound annual rate of about 20 percent and U.S. operating income at a compound annual rate in the mid-single digits, both measured over a five-year period.

Earlier, McDonald's reported a two percent drop in its U.S. operating income in the second quarter to $340.2 million. For the first six months of the year, U.S. operating income rose one percent to $611.4 million.

Outside the United States, operating income in the second quarter rose 10 percent to $416.8 million. That helped boost McDonald's net earnings for the quarter to a record $0.63 a share, in line with expectations, up from $0.59 a year ago.
Conley said foreign currency trimmed second quarter net earnings for McDonald's, whose nearly 22,000 units worldwide include more than 9,600 outside the United States.

Adjusted for constant foreign currency, second-quarter earnings per share would have been up 10 percent, he added. For the first six months, earnings per share would have risen 13 percent, compared with the 10 percent increase to $1.11 a share that was reported.

In the United States, McDonald's showed the effects of mixed results from its recent promotions. Conley said promotions thus far this year based on the Monopoly board game, the Teeny Beanie Baby toy giveaway and special prices for its Chicken McNuggets were successful.
The Campaign 55 promotion for lunch and dinner, which offered featured hamburgers for 55 cents, was "disappointing," Conley said.
"As we've go into the summer, we've got some momentum going for us with the 'Hercules' (movie tie-in) promotion and the 99-cent triple cheeseburger," Conley said.

McDonald's latest national promotion -- a tie-in with the "George of the Jungle" live action movie -- begins Friday. That promotion includes two Quarter Pounder hamburgers or two Sausage McMuffin with Egg breakfast sandwiches for $2.
